lacuna.name: paged-varlen-decode-sm75
lacuna.repo_anchor: plan/0007-d256-bridge/README.md, Out-of-scope line: "Out of scope: paged/varlen decode kernel (backlog), Triton/GDN kernel work, d=512 implementation." The gap is defined quantitatively in plan/0006-cu-sm80-on-sm75/retrospective.md: "per-(layer, request) python dispatch plus paged-KV gather copies outnumbered the real bridge kernels ~8:1 in kernel counts in the trace (1372 direct-copy + 448 index-put vs 224 bridge kernels), and decode pays a zero-padded 64-row Q tile. The fix list is known and recorded: a paged/varlen bridge kernel consuming block tables directly (removes gather and python loop in one stroke)". Reinforced in plan/0006 README item 5: "behind at short context (python dispatch + paged-KV gather; the varlen/paged bridge kernel is backlog)" and its correctness-gate section: "Remaining backlog unchanged: architectural backend speedup (paged/varlen kernel)".
lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09-07 no upstream serving stack ships a paged/varlen decode attention kernel for sm_75; what exists is a mix of one vendor library with an untested Turing path, two llama.cpp-family MMA-FA implementations with explicit Turing tables, and educational community kernels. (1) vLLM: the only paged-decode kernels that ever ran on cc 7.0+ in-tree (the original PageAttention v1/v2 behind the V0 FlashAttentionBackend, the code the vLLM paper ran on T4) were removed with V0 cleanup PR #25351 'Remove V0 attention backends' (closed 2025-09-21); the V1 selector auto-selects TRITON_ATTN on capability (7,5) because FLASH_ATTN and FLASHINFER are gated >= (8,0) (host plan/0006 record; corroborated by vLLM #38918: 'FLASH_ATTN is rejected at selection for compute capability'). vLLM #38918 (opened 2026-04-03, still current on v0.28.0 as of 2026-08-30) documents that on Turing the auto-selected TRITON_ATTN dies at kernel load with 'Required: 98304, Hardware limit: 65536' for Gemma4 (head_dim 512), fixed by #39018. (2) FlashInfer (arXiv 2501.01005, v1 2025-01-02, v2 2025-04-21, MLSys 2025): README claims 'Support for SM75 (Turing) and later'; sm75 was enabled by PR #449 'bugfix: Fix sm75 kernel configuration' (merged 2024-08-27, touching decode.cuh, prefill.cuh, sampling.cuh, mma.cuh), tracked from issue #160 ('Turing has been supported with PR #449. Volta currently has no supported plans'). Lead maintainer yzh119 in #1648 (2025-09-07): 'We have a subset of kernels that are compatible with SM75, the only issue is test coverage (we don't have a SM75 CI machine ...), but if user report related bugs we are happy to fix them.' Issue #3620 (opened 2026-06-12, OPEN, P1, repro flashinfer 0.6.12 on Tesla T4): BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCache fails first launch with CUDA invalid argument because the tile-size estimate omits k/v scale-factor buffers and SM75's 64 KB opt-in has no headroom; on SM80+ the 164 KB limit hides the miscount. The host's own gate-0 probe of 0.6.18 went further: prefill is silently wrong in every probed configuration (max_err up to 4.24), while decode (BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper) is correct - see sm75_viability. Current releases v0.6.18 (2026-08-29) and v0.6.18.post1 (2026-09-05); newer wheels JIT-compile sm75 kernels (no prebuilts). (3) llama.cpp: fattn-mma-f16.cuh carries an explicit TURING_MMA_AVAILABLE path with ggml_cuda_fattn_mma_get_config_turing() tables covering (DKQ,DV) = (256,256), (320,256), (512,512), (576,512) at ncols 8/16/32/64, falling through to the Ampere table otherwise - the only production-grade CUDA attention covering d=256..576/512 MLA tuples on Turing. The recent FA + quantized-KV long-prompt crash (#19036, opened 2026-01-23, closed 2026-01-24) is NOT Turing-specific: JohannesGaessler's root cause - 'The problem was introduced with PR #18986 because it made the V tensor non-contiguous which causes issues on dequantization for >= 65536 tokens. This should already be fixed on the latest master version by PR #19057.' (repro hardware was an RTX 3090, sm_86; q4_1, q4_0 AND q8_0 all failed past 65536 tokens). (4) ik_llama.cpp (CUDA floor 'Turing or newer'): FlashMLA / FlashMLA-2 / FlashMLA-3 are ikawrakow's own kernel generations, not DeepSeek's SM90/SM100-only library - PR 240 'Introducing FlashMLA - MLA with Flash Attention' (2025-03-03), PR 253 'FlashMLA-2 performance improvements' (2025-03-17), PR 265 'Allow Q8_0 KV cache with FlashMLA-2 on CUDA' (2025-03-12), PR 273/386 FlashMLA-3 on CUDA (Ampere+ required), PR 408 'slightly faster flash attention for DeepSeek models on CUDA, along with extending compatibility to Turing or newer GPUs' (2025-05-11) + PR 413 fix. Issue #1014 (2025-11-27, 2x Quadro RTX 8000, sm_75): the NEW MMA FA kernel crashed on Turing at cudaFuncSetAttribute (MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize) - the 64 KB block cap again; PR #1017 reverted the (192,128) DeepSeek MLA case to the original MMA on Turing; ikawrakow: 'Strictly speaking the new MMA FA should work on Turing, but I don't have a Turing GPU to debug, so that's why I just reverted it.' Issue #1142 (opened 2026-01-13, closed 2026-01-19): the q4_0/q4_1/q5_0 KV + FA corruption (q8_0/q6_0 fine) turned out to be the CPU FA fallback without GGML_IQK_FA_ALL_QUANTS, not a CUDA bug - 'I have the concept that all quantization types supported for KV cache should work on CUDA'. (5) Community SM75 kernels (JohnScheuer): flash-attention-sm75 (FlashAttention v1 forward, WMMA, fp16-only, d=64/128, decode 'falls back to PyTorch SDPA'; +27% end-to-end on Qwen2-0.5B, 31-33 -> 40-42 tok/s; ~1.4 TFLOPS kernel = ~5% of RTX 2070 peak; updated 2026-08-26); flash-attention-sm75-register-fused (2026-07-27; 5.0 TFLOPS full / 3.9-4.1 causal at d=64 only; still 3.6-4.0x slower than SDPA mem-efficient because the custom kernel is memory-bound at 29.3 FLOP/byte vs SDPA's compute-bound ~512); flash-decoding-bench (2026-07-19; chunked KV-parallel decode vs SDPA at q_len=1 on RTX 2070: chunked-parallel wins only above ~8K KV, 1.38x at kv=8192 bs=1, no benefit at bs=4; sequential Python chunking caps at 1.13x); no INT8-attention variant exists in any of the author's public repos (claim unverified). (6) Triton (which serves vLLM's TRITON_ATTN decode on sm75): tl.dot on Turing emitted Volta mma.884 at half of mma.1688 throughput even when it worked (triton #189); Volta+Turing support was dropped in Triton 3.3 via #5066, and tl.dot is broken for compute capability < 80 on Triton >= 3.3 (sglang #7467, Turing users unable to run Qwen3) - so the current in-engine decode attention on this hardware is FMA-scalar math unless Triton is pinned <= 3.2.
lacuna.sm75_viability: Measured on this host's TU102/Quadro RTX 6000 cards plus upstream Turing repros (Tesla T4 in FlashInfer #3620 and vLLM #38918; RTX 8000 in ik_llama.cpp #1014; RTX 2070 in the JohnScheuer benchmarks). What actually runs correctly on sm_75 today: (a) FlashInfer 0.6.18 decode via BatchDecodeWithPagedKVCacheWrapper under the paged contract (num_pages, 2, page_size, h, d): CORRECT by gate 0, max_err 0.00011-0.00049 across uniform/mixed/long KV batches, b up to 16, both kernel variants (plan/0006 retraction record) - the ONLY third-party paged decode kernel validated on this hardware; host-measured baseline (GQA 24/4, d=256): 16.2 tok/s b=1 kv=1024, 11.8 at kv=4096, 5.2 at kv=16384, 66.2 aggregate at b=8 kv=1024. Its prefill sibling is DISQUALIFIED (silently wrong, max_err up to 4.24). (b) The host's bridge kernel (d=64/128/256, k-chunked m16n8k8, 22.0-24.3 TFLOP/s at d=256) - correct and oracle-locked, but engine decode pays per-(layer, request) python dispatch + paged-KV gather (1372 direct-copy + 448 index-put vs 224 real kernels) and a zero-padded 64-row Q tile; that overhead is exactly this lacuna. (c) llama.cpp fattn-mma TURING tables (256/256 through 576/512) and ik_llama.cpp's 'original MMA' FA on Turing - existence proofs that deep-K MMA attention fits Turing's 64 KiB block budget when tiles are tuned per-arch. (d) SDPA mem-efficient (xformers-style) - correct fallback, used by the community kernels for decode. Attention-backend candidate matrix on sm_75: BRIDGE_ATTN (correct, fast kernel, no paged/varlen integration - this item); TRITON_ATTN (correct at d<=256 on current stacks but FMA-only math via Triton >= 3.3, and fails outright at d=512 needing 98 KiB smem - vLLM #38918); FLASH_ATTN / FA2 (gated __CUDA_ARCH__ >= 800; raw-binding probe on this card: d=256 launch failure cudaErrorInvalidValue - 64 KiB smem cap; d=128 RUNS but silently wrong, gate-0 max_err 2.20, DISQUALIFIED); FLASHINFER (decode-only correct; prefill disqualified); SDPA (correct, slower). Triton codegen path where it gates the item: on the lane's current toolchain Triton emits no tensor-core math for sm75 (dropped in 3.3, #5066; tl.dot broken on cc < 80, sglang #7467); pinned Triton <= 3.2 gets Volta mma.884 at half throughput; anything else is FMA - so a Triton-written paged decode kernel is not a real option, reinforcing a CUDA implementation in the existing flash_fwd_sm75.cuh. Real blockers, named: the 64 KiB per-block smem opt-in cap (recurs in FlashInfer #3620, FA2 d=256, ik_llama.cpp new-MMA crash, vLLM #38918 - every new tile config must re-prove it fits); no cp.async (Ampere+), no wgmma/TMA; ldmatrix IS native (Turing+) and the bridge already uses it; d=256 sits at 255/254 registers per lane (ptxas ceiling, zero spills, worth watching per the plan/0007 bisect). Fallback semantics: today the engine declines to TRITON_ATTN below the bridge's scope and FlashInfer decode remains the only vendor alternative; a failed paged-kernel arm must fall back to the current gather path, never to a silently-wrong kernel (gate 0). One design fact from the FlashInfer paper that de-risks the kernel: decode with query tile 1 runs on CUDA cores (tensor-core mma needs >= 16 rows) and is bandwidth-bound - so the decode-side paged kernel is a gather/indexing problem, not a tensor-core problem; the split-K/flash-decoding question (long-KV chunk parallelism) has a measured Turing crossover at ~8K KV for bs=1 and no benefit at bs=4 (flash-decoding-bench), so chunking is a long-context decision, not a default.
lacuna.upstream_base: Per-release last-good ledger lines the fork can rebase onto. FlashInfer: sm75 enablement = PR #449 'bugfix: Fix sm75 kernel configuration' (merged 2024-08-27; first shipped release v0.1.6 [uncertain]); supported-but-unverified status quo stated in #1648 (2025-09-07, no SM75 CI); prefill smem-accounting bug #3620 (opened 2026-06-12, still OPEN, P1; repro v0.6.12, T4); last-good for sm75 decode = v0.6.18 (2026-08-29, host gate-0 validated decode) with v0.6.18.post1 (2026-09-05) current. vLLM: V0 attention backends - the last in-tree paged-decode kernels that supported cc 7.0+ - removed by PR #25351 (closed 2025-09-21); since then no vendor paged decode path reaches sm_75 through the V1 selector (FLASH_ATTN/FLASHINFER gated >= (8,0)); Gemma4-class d=512 Triton smem failure #38918 (2026-04-03) with fix #39018, still current on v0.28.0 (2026-08-30). Triton: last release with Turing codegen = 3.2 (mma.884 at half throughput, triton #189); 3.3+ dropped Volta/Turing (#5066) and tl.dot is broken on cc < 80 (sglang #7467, 2025-06). llama.cpp: fattn-mma TURING_MMA_AVAILABLE config tables current at master (2026-09); FA + quantized-KV regression window PR #18986 (2026-01) -> fix PR #19057 (2026-01-24) after #19036. ik_llama.cpp: Turing FA compatibility PRs #408 + #413 (2025-05); new-MMA-on-Turing reverted by PR #1017 (2025-11-27) after #1014; CUDA floor documented 'Turing or newer' (FlashMLA-3 CUDA requires Ampere+). FlashAttention upstream: never shipped sm75 FA2 - 2.8.3's dormant sub-80 d=128 kernel is wrong (host gate-0 max_err 2.20 / plan-0006 record of ssiu fork traits fix), so there is no upstream FA release to rebase for this surface; the host's flash_fwd_sm75.cuh IS the base.

effort_value.effort_estimate: Full kernel-ladder campaign, not an adapter: (1) varlen Q packing in the existing decode launcher to kill the zero-padded 64-row tile (small - reuse flash_fwd_sm75.cuh unchanged, new host-side pack + per-request loop metadata); (2) in-kernel paged-KV indirection: consume the block table / KV page indices directly in the kernel under the (num_pages, 2, page_size, h, d) contract, removing the engine's gather copies and per-(layer, request) python dispatch (medium - index math plus staged loads inside the proven 64 KiB smem class; cp.async unavailable so double-buffer by hand as the kernel already does); (3) optional split-K / flash-decoding chunking for long-KV decode with deterministic LSE merge (larger, gated on measured need - the Turing crossover data says only contexts beyond ~8K at small batch benefit). Plus a BridgeAttentionBackend decode-path rewrite (one kernel launch per layer per step over the whole batch) and oracle/bench/test extensions. Rough size: a plan-sized arc comparable to a 0006/0007 stage - weeks of operator+lane time, no new external dependency; lands as a new entry pattern beside the existing templates ('dispatch extension is a new template instantiation, never a redesign').
effort_value.unlocks: Removes the measured 8:1 overhead tax (1372 gather copies + 448 index-puts vs 224 real kernels per trace window) on every engine step, converting the bridge from a parity-at-ctx2048 prefill curiosity into the default decode backend on sm_75 - the short-context ratios (0.11-0.71x vs TRITON recorded in plan/0006) are attributed precisely to this path. Unlocks: real TP2 decode throughput for the 27B hybrid (the operator's serving target, currently decode-bound with a still-open engine-level tp2 decode deficit whose bisect points at per-step scheduling/gather/allreduce interaction - the paged kernel removes one of the three suspects); GQA-packed decode without zero-padded tiles; long-context decode headroom (FlashInfer baseline shows 5.2 tok/s at kv=16384 - bandwidth-bound ceiling the in-kernel gather attacks); and, as a follow-on on the same indirection, in-kernel KV-cache dequant (q8_0 KV halves KV memory; llama.cpp proves quantized-KV FA on CUDA; ik_llama.cpp PR 265 proves q8_0 KV with its FA on CUDA). Also unblocks the macro-gate's decode rows ever moving above seeded without restart-lotto, since the engine-side variance source shrinks.
effort_value.dependency_order: Must land first (already in place): the plan/0007 kernel core - d=64/128/256 k-chunked templates, fp64 oracle, smem class, BridgeAttentionBackend dispatch, and the validated paged-cache contract (num_pages, 2, page_size, h, d) proven in the plan/0006 FlashInfer harness retraction. Before any timing: decode-shaped oracle extension (per-request seq_lens, mixed lengths, chunked prefix, magnitude cases) and a raw-tensor reference comparison that does NOT share its gather with the implementation (the plan/0006 vacuous-test lesson). Strongly advised before the campaign: close or fence the open tp2 engine-decode investigation (nsys/ncu instrument, plan/0007 bisect record) so the new kernel's A/B is not confounded by the same engine-level swings. Can proceed in parallel: FlashInfer decode baselines are recorded; varlen Q packing (item 1) is independent of block-table indirection (item 2); KV-quant in-kernel dequant is a follow-on gated on the plain paged kernel; split-K chunking is optional and separately gated.
effort_value.risk_notes: Correctness/numerics: (1) gather-index bugs are the historical failure class - plan/0006's backend unit tests passed vacuously because the fp64 reference consumed the SAME gather; the probe must compare against raw pre-gather tensors. (2) The silently-wrong precedent on sm75 is everywhere: FlashInfer 0.6.18 prefill (max_err 4.24), FA2 sub-80 d=128 (max_err 2.20), llama.cpp FA+quantized-KV (silent garbage past 65536 tokens between #18986 and #19057) - launch success proves nothing; gate 0 (assert, disqualify, never report wrong-tensor performance) is load-bearing. (3) fp16 softmax saturation regression class (raw dots ~1e5 vs 65504 ceiling) must be regression-locked with in_scale=100 oracle cases in every new entry pattern. (4) Split-K LSE merge changes accumulation order - bitwise equality with the non-paged kernel is unattainable; judge by oracle max_err profile + cross-backend PPL, not bit-equality. (5) smem: every tile/pipeline config must re-prove the 64 KiB opt-in (FlashInfer #3620's exact failure: estimate omitted scale-factor buffers; 0 headroom on sm75); d=256 already sits at 255/254 registers - watch ptxas spills on any new indexing arithmetic. Upstream-drift exposure: FlashInfer sm75 has no CI (their lead's own statement) so pinning it as the decode baseline is fragile; Triton may change FMA fallback behavior under TRITON_ATTN (the comparison arm); vLLM V1 selector and KV-manager layout changes (page_size, block-table format) can break the contract - the quilt/upstream checker discipline applies to the interface, not just kernels.
effort_value.determinism_class: Statistical, not bitwise, once chunking/split-K is in: accumulation and LSE-merge order differ from the gather-path kernel, and per-run batch composition reorders work; bitwise TP1-vs-TP2 greedy identity remains the engine-level check but kernel-level equality does not. Run-to-run variance sources on this host are dominated by an ENGINE-level mechanism, not the kernel: tp2 bridge decode swings 12.4-16.4 tok/s across restarts of the same kernel while the kernel-isolated A/B is stable (plan/0007 bisect record) - so decode rows must be judged on medians across >= 3 engine restarts (the recorded methodology fix). Copy the FlashInfer plan-phase determinism discipline: CPU-side planning with sorted longest-first priority-queue assignment, fixed workspace offsets, no atomics (their paper contrasts this with Stream-K's non-determinism) - it makes decode restart-stable and CUDAGraph-capturable, which the engine wants anyway. Gate discipline to hold: fp64 oracle max_err profile must match the existing d<=256 profile before any timing exists; median-of-N (N >= 3 restarts for tp2 arms); control arm inside every campaign; PPL within the 0.5% cross-backend gate with the fp16-exp2 softmax cost explicitly named if it moves.

decision.priority_signal: For: it is the recorded architectural fix for the measured short-context deficit (0.11-0.71x vs TRITON), with the kernel core already built, oracle-locked, and fast (22-24.3 TFLOP/s at d=256) - the remaining work is indirection and packing, not new physics; every third-party decode option on sm75 is degraded or wrong (FlashInfer prefill silently wrong, FA2 wrong/unlaunchable, Triton FMA-only since 3.3, V0 paged attention deleted from vLLM), so the bridge is the only path to a correct AND fast decode attention on this hardware; llama.cpp's TURING tables and FlashInfer's correct-on-sm75 decode prove both the deep-K and the paged-contract halves are feasible; the bandwidth-bound nature of decode (FlashInfer paper: decode = q-tile 1 on CUDA cores) means the win comes from removing 8:1 gather traffic, which is measurable and mechanistic. Against: decode being bandwidth-bound also caps the ceiling - gather copies may already overlap compute, so the realized win could be well under the kernel-count ratio suggests (must measure); the tp2 engine-decode anomaly is still open and would confound any A/B until instrumented; FlashInfer decode already provides a correct paged-decode fallback, so the marginal urgency vs wiring FlashInfer decode behind the bridge is a real alternative (weaker: leaves prefill on the bridge with a mixed stack, depends on an unCI'd vendor path, and surrenders KV-quant and packing control). Window-closing risk is real and one-directional: Triton dropped Turing (3.3+), vLLM deleted its cc-7.0 paged kernels (PR #25351), FlashInfer admits no SM75 CI - the ecosystem will not produce this kernel; if this host wants paged decode on sm75 it must write it.
decision.recommended_probe: Cheapest gate-0 probe (oracle-checked, no timing until numerics proven): extend fwd_oracle.cu with decode-shaped paged cases - B requests, mixed seq_lens including chunked prefixes, block table over (num_pages, 2, page_size, h, d) at page_size 16 and 32, d=128 GQA 6:1 - then implement ONLY the in-kernel block-table gather plus varlen Q packing around the EXISTING d=128 template (no split-K, no d=256). Pass criteria: (a) max_err vs the fp64 oracle identical in profile to the non-paged kernel across all mixed-length and in_scale=100 magnitude cases; (b) a second reference built from RAW pre-gather tensors (not sharing the kernel's indirection) agrees - the vacuous-test guard; (c) ptxas: zero spills, smem unchanged in class (<= 64 KiB opt-in asserted at launch). Only after (a)-(c): one nsys count on a 27B engine decode step showing direct-copy/index-put kernels dropping from 1372+448 toward 0 and one kernel launch per layer per step; timing and macro-gate rows after that. Settles: whether block-table indirection is numerically free on this kernel and whether the gather tax was real latency or overlapped - both in one probe, on hardware in hand.
